_note: Signatures for ts-bench v1 exercises. Exercism stubs mostly say `unknown` or have no parameters, so a stub-derived F is useless as a contract. Each `type` below was written by hand from the call sites in the exercise's test file (argument and expectation shapes only, never a solution). OpenArc (A/B/C) and the baseline (D) get exactly the same typed signatures. `types` holds extra project-local types the signature needs. `sets` splits the function exercises into a dev set (prompt tuning) and a held-out test set (final check only). Rule, deterministic: each exercise gets one hand-assigned category (text: string transforms/ciphers/parsing; generate: verse/number-to-text output; numeric; structure: arrays/matrices/maps/search); within a category, exercises are taken in order of Exercism track difficulty (config.json), then slug; the nine evolve-multi exercises (acronym, binary-search, diamond, flatten-array, rectangles, spiral-matrix, transpose, variable-length-quantity, wordy) are pinned to dev, and each remaining exercise goes to whichever set has fewer non-pinned members of its category so far (ties to test). Never tune on `test`.

fns.convert: (digits: number[], inputBase: number, outputBase: number) => number[]

flatten-array.types: export interface Nested extends Array<number | null | undefined | Nested> {}
flatten-array._note: interface form on purpose: the equivalent `type Nested = Array<number | null | undefined | Nested>` makes open-arc 0.6.3's Example<F> fail with TS2589 on the spec itself (pilot run used it; see results/2026-10-31-untuned-ollama-pilot/summary.md)

knapsack.types: export interface Item { weight: number; value: number }

nucleotide-count.types: export interface NucleotideCounts { A: number; C: number; G: number; T: number }

fns.degreesOfSeparation: (familyTree: FamilyTree, personA: string, personB: string) => number

saddle-points.types: export interface Point { row: number; column: number }
